name: Optimazz – Website Optimization and Speedup
author: Shipon Karmakar

sections.description:
Optimazz is an all-in-one performance suite that applies the optimizations with the biggest impact on Core Web Vitals — automatically and safely. Every module is opt-in and reversible, and Optimazz never overwrites another caching plugin’s files.

Modules included:

  • Page Cache — serve static HTML instead of running PHP on every request, with smart exclusions (logged-in users, carts, query strings), automatic purging on content changes, and a cron-based cache preloader so visitors never hit a cold page.
  • JavaScript — defer scripts and delay them until the first user interaction to cut Total Blocking Time, with an exclusion list.
  • CSS — minify, combine, and load CSS asynchronously to remove render-blocking stylesheets.
  • Image Optimization — lazy-load images and iframes, add missing dimensions to prevent layout shift, generate and serve WebP/AVIF, bulk-compress your existing library, convert opaque PNGs to JPEG, and replace YouTube embeds with a click-to-load preview.
  • Fonts — add font-display: swap, preconnect to font hosts, and preload font files.
  • Database — clean revisions, auto-drafts, trashed posts, spam/trashed comments and expired transients, optimize tables, and schedule automatic cleanups.
  • Heartbeat — reduce or disable the WordPress Heartbeat API per context to lower server load.
  • Tweaks — disable emojis, embeds, dashicons, query strings, XML-RPC and pingbacks, and add DNS-prefetch / preconnect hints.
  • CDN — rewrite static asset URLs to your CDN hostname.

A live performance score on the dashboard shows which optimizations are active and your biggest remaining win.

Build process and source code

The admin interface is a React application. The human-readable source lives in the src/ directory shipped inside the plugin (src/index.js and src/index.scss), and the compiled, minified output lives in build/.

To regenerate the compiled files from source:

  1. Install dependencies: npm install
  2. Build: npm run build

This uses the official @wordpress/scripts (webpack) toolchain — no custom or hidden build configuration. All source and build tooling are included in the plugin; nothing is obfuscated.

External services

Optimazz does not require any external service to function, and it works entirely on your own server by default. Two optional, admin-controlled features can reference third-party hosts:

  1. Google Fonts optimization (Fonts module). If — and only if — your theme or another plugin already loads Google Fonts, and you enable the Fonts module, Optimazz adds preconnect resource hints to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com and can add display=swap to the existing font URL. Optimazz does not add Google Fonts to a site that isn’t already using them, and it does not send any personal or site data — a preconnect is only a browser hint to open a connection earlier. The fonts themselves are requested by the visitor’s browser from Google, exactly as they were before the plugin, under Google’s terms: https://policies.google.com/terms and privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

  2. CDN rewriting (CDN module). If you enable the CDN module and enter a CDN hostname, Optimazz rewrites the URLs of your own static assets (CSS, JS, images) to that hostname so visitors’ browsers load them from your CDN. The CDN is a service you choose and configure; Optimazz sends no data to it itself and is not affiliated with any CDN provider. Consult your chosen CDN’s own terms and privacy policy.

Both features are off by default and take effect only after you explicitly enable them.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the optimazz folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it from the Plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress.
  3. Open Optimazz in the admin menu and enable the modules you want.
sections.faq:
Does Optimazz work alongside another caching plugin?

Optimazz will not overwrite another caching plugin’s advanced-cache.php drop-in. To use Optimazz page caching, deactivate any other page-caching plugin first. The other (non-caching) modules work alongside most plugins.

Will page caching work on my host?

Page caching needs WP_CACHE to be defined, which Optimazz adds to wp-config.php automatically. If wp-config.php is not writable, Optimazz shows a notice with the line to add manually.

Is it safe to delay JavaScript?

Delay-until-interaction is the biggest speed win but can affect scripts that must run before interaction. Start with “Delay” on and “Delay all” off, then add any problematic script keywords to the exclusion list.

Does converting PNG to JPEG lose my originals?

Only opaque PNGs are converted, the original is optionally backed up to uploads/optimazz-backup, and the conversion is rolled back if anything fails.

Does the plugin phone home or collect data?

No. Optimazz does not track users, register accounts, or send any of your site’s or visitors’ data to Optimazz servers. See the “External services” section for the only optional third-party hints the plugin can add.

Why does the plugin add inline <script> and <style> tags to my pages?

Those small inline fragments (the delay-JavaScript loader, critical/async CSS, the lazy-load helper and LCP preload hints) are the actual optimization output that Optimazz writes into your front-end HTML. They are the product of the plugin’s work, not the plugin’s own asset loading — a delay-until-interaction loader cannot be enqueued as an external file. The admin interface and all of the plugin’s own assets are loaded normally through the WordPress enqueue functions.
sections.changelog:
1.0.24

  • Fixed: the automatic preload (after saving settings, and the scheduled one) only warmed the first 50 addresses, so on bigger sites it covered far fewer pages than a manual preload. It now warms the whole site in short background chunks — each continues where the last stopped, and only one runs at a time — so it never overloads the server or hits the PHP time limit.
  • Improved: preloading is much faster — desktop and mobile copies are warmed at the same time, a manual preload warms several pages per step, and the page list is built once per run instead of on every step.
  • Improved: the preload explains what it is warming, e.g. “Found 74 pages to warm: 10 pages, 11 posts, 18 products, 12 category and tag pages” — the total includes posts, products and archive pages, not only Pages. Page-builder template libraries (Elementor, Beaver Builder, Divi, Bricks …), WooCommerce cart / checkout / account pages and anything in “Never cache these URLs” are no longer in the list, since visitors never get them from the cache.
  • Fixed: the preloader reported pages as “warmed” even when none were saved to the cache (e.g. “Warmed 114 / 121” while Cached pages stayed at 0), with no hint why. It now counts only pages that really reached the cache (“· 98 cached · 16 not cached”) — counted per page (desktop and mobile copies of one page count once), so it matches the “Cached pages” card, and when pages are not being cached it stops after a few and explains the exact reason and fix: another caching plugin owns advanced-cache.php, the drop-in or WP_CACHE is missing, a server or CDN cache (LiteSpeed, Cloudflare, Varnish …) answers before WordPress, a plugin sets DONOTCACHEPAGE, pages return an error status, the cache folder is not writable, or your exclusion rules match.
  • Fixed: on sites behind a proxy, load balancer or Cloudflare (HTTPS ends at the proxy), cached pages were saved under an http address and never found again for https visitors. The real scheme is now read from X-Forwarded-Proto / CF-Visitor.
  • New: if another caching plugin (WP Rocket, Seraphinite Accelerator, LiteSpeed Cache …) controls the cache drop-in while Optimazz page cache is on, a notice now appears on every admin screen — naming the plugin, with one-click “Deactivate it and use Optimazz” and “Use Optimazz for caching” buttons, or “Keep the other plugin” to hide it. Before, the Optimazz page cache silently stayed inactive unless you opened its Cache health panel.
  • Improved: conflict detection now also recognises Seraphinite Accelerator, FlyingPress, WP-Optimize and NitroPack, and cache plugins installed under a renamed folder (e.g. a GitHub download).
  • Improved: “Cache lifespan” and “Auto-preload” can now be changed right from the Dashboard (a dropdown on each row), and the preload row shows when the next run is due.
  • Fixed: scheduled auto-preload often never ran on well-cached sites. WordPress only runs scheduled tasks when it loads, but cached pages are served without loading WordPress, so the preload quietly went overdue. When a preload is due, a cached page view now wakes WordPress’s scheduler in the background (after the page has been sent, at most once a minute).
  • Fixed: the dashboard showed an overdue preload as “in 3 hours”; it now says “due now”, and a new “Last auto-preload” line shows when it last ran and how many pages it warmed (or that a firewall blocked it).
  • New: choose how often the automatic preload runs — every hour, twice a day or once a day (Preload settings). Turning page caching off now also clears the preload schedule, and a notice explains when WP-Cron is disabled on the site.
  • Fixed: switching a module on or off (or using Undo, Reset, or the post-update refresh) cleared the whole page cache and then left it empty, so the site ran uncached — and slow — until each page happened to get a visitor or the twice-daily preload ran. The cache is now rebuilt automatically straight after (when page cache and preloading are on).
  • Fixed: switching Optimazz page caching off, or deactivating Optimazz, turned off WP_CACHE even when another caching plugin (e.g. WP Rocket) owned the cache drop-in, which silently disabled that plugin’s page cache. WP_CACHE is now only turned off when the drop-in was Optimazz’s own.
  • Fixed: cache preloading stopped with a 403 error when a firewall such as the 6G/7G rules in All-In-One Security was enabled. The preloader identified itself as “Optimazz-Preloader”, and these firewalls block any visitor whose user-agent contains the word “loader”. It now identifies as “Optimazz-CacheWarmer” in the standard crawler format, which those rules allow. The user-agent can be changed with the new optimazz_preload_user_agent filter.

1.0.23

  • Fixed: with WebP/AVIF serving on, some images (often the site logo) showed as broken on HTTPS sites whose content still used old http:// image addresses. Browsers upgrade a plain http:// image to https:// automatically, but block an http:// image inside a source — and never fall back. Next-gen image sources now always use https:// on HTTPS pages.
  • Fixed: in responsive images, a size without a WebP/AVIF copy could be offered to the browser and show as broken; only sizes whose next-gen file exists are now listed.
  • Fixed: tidier image markup — no attributes added after a self-closing slash, and no duplicate decoding/fetchpriority attributes.
  • New: Google Fonts optimization (Fonts module). Page builders such as Elementor load every Google Font family as a separate request, each with every weight from 100 to 900 plus italics. Optimazz now merges them into a single request and loads only the weights and styles your pages actually use (weights 400 and 700 are always kept). On a typical Elementor site this turns three render-blocking requests into one and cuts the font CSS by more than half (measured: 170 KB down to 64 KB). Both options are on by default and can be switched off in the Fonts settings; requests that subset by text are never changed.
  • Improved: the build tooling (package.json) ships with the plugin again, so the admin interface can be rebuilt from the included source as described under “Build process and source code”.
  • Fixed: with the CDN module on, CSS minify/combine, WebP delivery and missing-image-dimension fixes were silently skipped, because the CDN rewrite ran before the other optimizations and they could no longer recognise your own files. The CDN rewrite now runs last, on the finished page.
  • Improved: when the update safety check switches Safe Mode on to protect a site, it now keeps re-checking and switches Safe Mode back off by itself as soon as pages load correctly again, restoring full optimization (CSS combine, async CSS and JavaScript delay). Previously Safe Mode stayed on until someone turned it off manually, so a site could quietly run slower for a long time after a temporary problem. If pages break again within a day of being restored, Safe Mode stays on and the admin decides. Safe Mode that you switch on yourself is never changed automatically.
  • Fixed: the update safety check now also recognises stylesheets served from your CDN hostname (when the CDN module is on), so a page that loads unstyled through the CDN is detected instead of being reported as healthy.
  • Fixed: the “Optimazz Safe Mode is on” notice no longer lingers after Safe Mode was switched off via Undo last change, Reset or Import.
  • Fixed: uninstalling Optimazz now removes all of its data, including the version marker, the safety-check state and its scheduled check, and the cached font-weight data.

1.0.22

  • Fixed: on some hosts (certain LiteSpeed/WAF setups and managed hosts) pages loaded unstyled because the server does not serve — or routinely deletes — files under wp-content/cache/, which is where Optimazz kept its generated CSS. Since the page HTML references those files by name, a page that could not load them rendered without styling. Optimazz now stores generated CSS under wp-content/uploads/optimazz/ instead — the standard, always-served, persistent location page builders also use — so the stylesheets load reliably and are never wiped out from under a cached page. On update the page cache is refreshed automatically so pages pick up the new location with no manual step.
  • New: update safety guard. Shortly after the plugin updates, Optimazz quietly checks its own front page to confirm the optimized CSS actually loads. If it finds pages rendering unstyled — their generated stylesheets returning 404, usually because an external server or CDN cache is still serving old pages — it automatically switches on Safe Mode to keep the site working (pausing the risky CSS/JS transforms without changing your saved settings, so pages fall back to their original stylesheets) and shows an admin notice explaining what happened. After you clear your server/CDN cache and switch Safe Mode off from Tools, Optimazz re-checks and re-protects the site if anything is still broken — so an update can no longer leave a site visibly broken.

1.0.21

  • Fixed: after updating, a site whose page cache was already populated could keep serving pages that loaded unstyled, until the cache was purged by hand. A plugin update never clears the page cache, so any HTML cached by an earlier version — still pointing at combined CSS/JS files that an older purge had removed — stayed in place and rendered without styling. Optimazz now clears the page cache automatically once, the first time it runs after an update, and re-aligns its caching drop-in; the generated CSS/JS assets are kept, so pages come back fully styled on the next visit with no manual purge needed. This completes the 1.0.20 fix for existing installs.

1.0.20

  • Fixed: pages could intermittently load completely unstyled when CSS minify/combine was on together with page caching (or a server-level cache such as LiteSpeed). Optimazz names each generated CSS/JS file by a content hash and embeds those filenames in the cached HTML — but purging the page cache also deleted those generated files, so any HTML still held in a cache (Optimazz’s own, a CDN’s, or the server’s) pointed at stylesheets that had been removed, returning 404 and rendering the page without styling until they regenerated. Purging the page cache now preserves the hashed CSS/JS assets (they are self-invalidating — a source change produces a new filename), keeping the HTML and its stylesheets consistent.

1.0.19

  • Fixed: page caching could silently stop working after a plugin update or a manual re-upload, making the whole site slow (every request fell back to full PHP). The advanced-cache.php drop-in embeds the path to the cache engine, and if the plugin folder was moved or recreated by the update, that path went stale — but Optimazz still recognised the drop-in as its own and never repaired it. Optimazz now detects a stale drop-in and rewrites it with the correct path automatically, and the drop-in itself falls back to the standard plugin location so caching keeps working immediately. If you were affected, the cache heals itself on the first page view after updating.
  • Improved: the per-request cache readiness check no longer spins up the WordPress filesystem API just to read its own drop-in, removing needless overhead on every uncached request.

1.0.18

  • New: Safe Mode (Tools screen). If a theme or page builder looks broken after you enable optimization, one toggle pauses just the riskiest transforms — combine CSS, async CSS, remove-block-CSS and JavaScript delay — while keeping page cache, minify, defer and lazy-load running. It changes nothing in your saved settings; those optimizations simply pause until you switch Safe Mode off, so recovery is instant and reversible. Filterable via optimazz_safe_mode so a host can force it on during an incident.
  • New: Undo last change (Tools screen). Optimazz now keeps a one-step backup of your settings taken before every save, reset or Safe Mode toggle, so a single click restores the previous state — and undo is itself reversible (press it again to redo).

Older versions

The complete history (1.0.0 onward) is in changelog.txt, included with the plugin.

upgrade_notice.1.0.24: Scheduled cache preloading now runs on time even when every visitor gets a cached page, works behind 6G/7G firewalls, and the cache rebuilds itself after you change settings. Also warns you when another caching plugin is blocking the Optimazz page cache. Recommended.
upgrade_notice.1.0.15: Adds a Dashboard "Recommendations" panel that tells you exactly what to optimize next, with one-click fixes. Fully local — no external service. Recommended.
upgrade_notice.1.0.14: Reduce Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS): a new Font loading "Optional" mode removes web-font layout shift, and images/iframes now reserve their space with aspect-ratio. Recommended for a better Core Web Vitals score.
upgrade_notice.1.0.13: Image optimization is more robust — WebP/AVIF conversion no longer crashes on large images, bulk jobs skip a single failed item instead of stopping, and a new Server Requirements panel (Tools) shows exactly what your host supports. Recommended.
upgrade_notice.1.0.12: The cache preloader is now firewall-friendly — it paces its requests and stops immediately if a firewall or security plugin returns 403/429/503, so warming can no longer trip a rate-limiter. Recommended.
upgrade_notice.1.0.11: Smarter cache preloading — warming now follows the whole site like a sitemap (custom post types and category/tag archives too, most-important first) with a live time-remaining estimate. Recommended.
upgrade_notice.1.0.10: Adds opt-in "Remove unused CSS" options (block-editor CSS on the front end, WooCommerce and Easy Digital Downloads CSS off their own pages) that cut render-blocking CSS and improve First Contentful Paint, plus a refreshed sidebar and a fix for admin scroll flicker. Recommended.
upgrade_notice.1.0.9: Adds a one-click "Take over caching" fix for when another caching plugin blocks Optimazz — installs the drop-in and enables WP_CACHE so pages are actually cached. Recommended if Cache health shows a conflict.
upgrade_notice.1.0.8: Important mobile speed fix: the hero (LCP) image is no longer lazy-loaded, so Largest Contentful Paint is faster after activation — the main cause of "my site got slower." Also delays third-party scripts (analytics, pixels, chat) to cut mobile blocking time, adds a one-click "Cache health" check, and warns when optimizing without Page Cache. Strongly recommended.
upgrade_notice.1.0.7: Fixes bulk WebP/AVIF conversion and preload failing with "not a valid JSON response" on low-memory hosts (conversion now adapts to the memory limit and processes one image at a time when needed), and makes LCP image preloading smarter — no more preloading the logo or an oversized image, which could slow some sites after 1.0.5. Recommended update.
upgrade_notice.1.0.6: Fixes a layout break when "Combine CSS" is enabled on page-builder sites (mega-menus and sections no longer lose their styling), and adds a progress panel to database optimization. Recommended update.
upgrade_notice.1.0.5: Important fix: WooCommerce checkout is now safe on default settings (never cached or JS-delayed). Also: delaying JavaScript no longer slows First/Largest Contentful Paint on JavaScript-rendered sites. Also adds inline JS minification, a Critical CSS field, LCP preload, and cleaner settings.
upgrade_notice.1.0.4: Fixes two possible fatal errors during image optimization, adds separate defer/delay exclusion lists, and polishes the admin interface. Recommended update.
upgrade_notice.1.0.3: Important fix for Apache and LiteSpeed servers, where optimized CSS could be blocked and leave pages unstyled. Also includes a cache-key security fix. Upgrading is recommended.
upgrade_notice.1.0.1: Compatibility and code-quality improvements for the plugin directory review.

screenshots.caption: Dashboard — live performance score, cache statistics, quick actions, and per-module on/off switches.
Page Cache — serve static HTML instead of running PHP, with separate mobile caching.
File Optimization — defer and delay JavaScript, and minify, combine and async-load CSS.
Media — lazy-load images and iframes, add missing dimensions, and convert to WebP/AVIF.
Fonts — font-display swap, preconnect to font hosts, and preload font files.
Preload — warm the cache automatically so visitors never hit a cold page.
Advanced Rules — fine-tune caching with URL, cookie, and user-agent exclusions.
Database — clean revisions, drafts, spam, and transients, and optimize tables.
Heartbeat — reduce or disable the WordPress Heartbeat API to lower server load.
Tweaks — disable emojis, embeds, query strings, XML-RPC, and other front-end bloat.
CDN — rewrite static asset URLs to your CDN hostname.
Tools — import, export, and reset your configuration.
